recent_posts.title: When trying to make a team better gets you blamed for its failures
recent_posts.summary: A 28-year veteran tester reflects on a recent professional experience where her efforts to improve a team's quality practices backfired. Framed as a 'test automation engineer' in an agile team, her authentic, persistent approach—intended to help—was perceived as harmful to the team. She explores the tension between being a catalyst for quality and becoming a 'canary in the coal mine': powerless to fix systemic issues yet absorbing the blame for them. The post raises open questions about whether experienced testers should invest more in preparation, walk away earlier, or learn to suppress their instincts when the context demands it.

recent_posts.title: A Seasoned Tester's Crystal Ball: Stop with the prompting, be clear on your intent
recent_posts.summary: A seasoned tester draws parallels between intentional programming, test-driven development, and modern AI prompting. The core argument is that 'prompt engineering' is really just the age-old practice of clearly expressing intent — something good testers and developers have always done. Rather than chasing prompt engineering techniques, the author advocates for focusing on clearly articulating what you actually want, using examples where helpful, and recognizing that AI tools already have context engineering baked in that may override your prompting attempts anyway.

recent_posts.title: Why AI should find bugs directly instead of generating test cases
recent_posts.summary: A seasoned testing professional argues that generating test cases with AI misses the point entirely. Testing is about finding information, not executing step-by-step instructions. Exploratory testing principles show that asking AI directly for bugs yields better results than generating test cases. The author introduces the concept of 'Test Intelligence Mesh' at CGI Finland, which packages contemporary exploratory testing skills with AI assistance to produce valuable testing outcomes rather than documentation artifacts.

recent_posts.title: A Seasoned Tester's Crystal Ball
recent_posts.summary: A seasoned testing consultant shares two real-world productivity improvement stories. The first (4x) examines how a tester working at 50% capacity delivered double the output compared to full-time work a year earlier, attributed to accumulated domain knowledge, risk-based testing, and specification involvement. The second (13x) compares two phases of test automation work, where GitHub Copilot agentic use was introduced in the second phase. The author concludes the dramatic improvement came primarily from learning and accumulated context rather than the AI tool itself, while noting risks like drift in quality under pressure.

recent_posts.title: A Seasoned Tester's Crystal Ball: Requirements lead into worse testing?
recent_posts.summary: Providing testers with predefined requirements, test cases, or automation can paradoxically limit testing effectiveness. When given requirements, testers often stop after verifying them without considering completeness or exploring beyond constraints. Without constraints, testers default to whatever previous stakeholders requested. Experienced testers learn to test both with and without requirements, but this skill isn't intuitive for newcomers who mistakenly view requirements as making testing easier when they actually create false stopping criteria.

recent_posts.title: A Seasoned Tester's Crystal Ball: Benchmarking results
recent_posts.summary: A seasoned tester benchmarked different testing approaches on the same application: solo human testing found 62% of issues, human-with-AI collaboration found 100%, AI-with-human-prompting found 55%, pure AI found 5%, and 57 average human testers found 18%. The experiment used GitHub Copilot with Claude Opus 4.5 and Playwright, demonstrating that AI augmentation significantly improves testing effectiveness when properly guided, but AI alone performs poorly.

recent_posts.title: A Seasoned Tester's Crystal Ball: Quality adventures vibe coding for light production
recent_posts.summary: A tester shares their experience rapidly building an enrollment application using AI-assisted coding ("vibe coding") and deploying it directly to production. The post catalogs various bugs discovered through real-world usage: Safari rendering issues, boundary condition errors, incomplete feature removal, missing database retry logic, local storage overwriting database data, poor error handling, security misconfigurations, and data loss. The application served 38 users with 2 encountering issues, providing practical lessons on testing in production and the pitfalls of AI-generated code.

recent_posts.title: A Seasoned Tester's Crystal Ball
recent_posts.summary: Consulting services differ not just in deliverables but in the relationship and additional value provided. Three consultants with different billing approaches (full hours, half hours, and managed hours) can deliver similar value, but the cost-to-value ratio varies based on what's included "for free" in the relationship. The distinction between the service itself (the box) and the relationship that transforms it (the arrow) matters more than simple hour comparisons. Understanding what extras come with a service—like systematic executive interviews, training, or relationship management—provides better insight for evaluating and comparing professional services.

recent_posts.title: Understanding and closing the results gap in software testing
recent_posts.summary: The "results gap" represents the difference in testing outcomes between groups with similar responsibilities. Effective testing means finding relevant issues others missed, not just executing checklists. This gap emerges from differences in time investment, domain knowledge, and environment access. Reducing it requires coaching, team agreements, and collaborative practices like pairing to fix bugs at their root cause. Contemporary exploratory testing combines testing, programming, and collaboration to systematically minimize this gap and deliver meaningful quality feedback before production.

recent_posts.title: A Seasoned Tester's Crystal Ball: Learning, and why agency matters
recent_posts.summary: Effective learning requires agency and active engagement, not passive consumption. A workplace training session on GitHub Copilot revealed that attendees who zoned out couldn't share a single insight afterward. True learning means being able to demonstrate new skills or knowledge, not just awareness. Testers should take control of their learning by choosing formats that work for them, actively seeking takeaways, and ensuring time invested produces tangible results. Naming your learning strategies and techniques enables better control and explainability of your development process.
